channel.title: Bloomberg — diagnostic source feed
channel.description: Diagnostic feed grouped by acquisition connector.

item.title: Morgan Stanley Banker in Australia Says Bathla Is ‘Hammer Blow’
item.description: Morgan Stanley’s investment banking chief in Australia said the collapse of Bathla Group will have significant impacts on the economy at a time when sliding house prices could curb consumer spending.
item.dc:creator: Adam Haigh

item.title: Bathla Seeks Stopgap Funds as $2.5 Billion Debt Crisis Escalates
item.description: Bathla Group, the insolvent Australian property developer that’s shaken the nation’s real estate and private credit market, faces new tests at the start of the week.
item.dc:creator: Richard Henderson

item.title: Japan's Go President Eyes Expansion in Asia, Robotaxis
item.description: Go, the taxi booking app operator that pulled off Japan’s biggest initial public offering this year, is eyeing ways to expand domestically and across Asia, and doesn't see competitors like Uber as a threat. Go President Hiroshi Nakajima spoke exclusively with Bloomberg's Shery Ahn about Japan's unique ride-hailing market and future opportunities like robotaxis. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Japan Likely Sold Treasuries to Fund Record Yen Intervention
item.description: Japan likely sold a portion of its holdings of foreign securities, including US Treasuries, to finance its record currency intervention over the past month.
item.dc:creator: Erica Yokoyama

item.title: China Injects Billions of Capital Into Banks, Insurers
item.description: China is injecting billions into its largest banks and insurers to shore up balance sheets and sustain growth in a slowing economy. Bloomberg's Sunny Bangia explains. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Goldman’s Moe Sees 80% Upside for Korean Stocks on Memory Boom
item.description: A Goldman Sachs Group Inc. strategist is standing by his bullish target for South Korean stocks, saying investors underestimate how long the AI boost for the nation’s memory chipmakers will last.
item.dc:creator: Sangmi Cha

item.title: Gold Holds Drop as US Jobs, Hormuz Strikes Boost Rate-Hike Case
item.description: Gold held a decline, after stronger-than-expected US payrolls data and escalating tensions in the Middle East raised the prospects for an interest-rate hike as early as next week.
item.dc:creator: Robin Paxton

item.title: Asian Stocks Gain on Tech, Oil Rises After Attacks: Markets Wrap
item.description: Asian stocks rose after US technology shares advanced on Friday. Oil climbed after the US and Iran traded tanker attacks in the Strait of Hormuz.
item.dc:creator: Nicholas Reynolds

item.title: Latest Oil Market News and Analysis for September 7
item.description: Oil climbed after the US attacked Iranian tankers and Tehran declared a new restricted zone outside the Strait of Hormuz, raising concerns about prolonged disruptions to energy flows through the waterway.
item.dc:creator: Bingyan Wang

item.title: Bond Traders Brace for More Swings at Both Ends of US Yield Curve
item.description: US bond investors are preparing for more turbulence across the maturity spectrum, with potential catalysts in the week ahead that may trigger big moves for both short- and long-term securities.
item.dc:creator: Greg Ritchie and Elizabeth Stanton

item.title: Bloomberg This Weekend 09/06/2026
item.description: The news doesn’t stop when markets close. Hosts David Gura, Christina Ruffini and Lisa Mateo bring clarity, context and a bit of humor to the weekend’s biggest headlines, LIVE from New York. Joined by BBC Chief International Correspondent Lyse Doucet, AFL-CIO President Liz Shuler, Michigan Rep. Haley Stevens and California Rep. Kevin Kiley. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Pointed! Bloomberg's Weekly News Quiz For Risk-Takers
item.description: Pointed offers a strategic twist to the news quiz format, testing not just players’ knowledge of the news but also their confidence in their answers. Join Bloomberg's Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini, and Jeff Mason as they play and check out the quiz for yourself at Bloomberg.com (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: NBA Hits Clippers With Historic Penalties
item.description: The NBA fined the Los Angeles Clippers $30 million and stripped the franchise of five first-round draft picks after an independent investigation found the team circumvented salary-cap rules by facilitating off-court income opportunities for Kawhi Leonard. Bloomberg News Senior Sports Reporter Randall Williams joins Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason on Bloomberg This Weekend and explains that owner Steve Ballmer was also suspended for a year, while Leonard was fined $700,000 in one of the league’s most severe disciplinary actions. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Rep. Stevens Says Canadian Tariffs Are Squeezing Michigan
item.description: On Bloomberg This Weekend, Michigan Representative Haley Stevens (D) says escalating US tariffs on Canadian goods are raising costs and creating uncertainty for manufacturers in her district, with the deeply integrated auto supply chain particularly exposed. Stevens tells hosts Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason that she is promoting legislation that would provide households with as much as $1,700 to offset tariff-related costs, while criticizing the Trump administration’s approach to trade with Canada. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: British Food Is Having a US Moment
item.description: British food is enjoying new popularity in the US, with a wave of pub-inspired restaurants drawing crowds with traditional dishes served in more modern settings. Bloomberg Pursuits Contributing Restaurant Columnist Oliver Guy and Anchor of Daybreak Europe Caroline Hepker sit down with Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason on Bloomberg This Weekend and say social media, travel and demand for affordable comfort food are helping fuel the trend, with New York’s Dean’s among the restaurants putting classics such as stargazy pie and bubble and squeak back in the spotlight. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: USS Lincoln Sailors Describe Toll of Deployment
item.description: The USS Abraham Lincoln’s crew received a long-awaited port visit in Thailand after a 286-day deployment that included a modern-era record of 264 consecutive days at sea and months of combat operations in the Middle East. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend is Bloomberg News Southeast Asia Reporter Philip Heijmans who recently returned from Thailand and says sailors described food shortages, limited communications with family and uncertainty over their return, while many also expressed pride in their mission. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Races to Boost Missile Interceptor Output
item.description: The US retains significant munitions capacity for operations against Iran, but stocks of sophisticated interceptors missiles have come under greater pressure. Bloomberg Intelligence Senior Defense Analyst Col. Wayne Sanders tells tells Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason on Bloomberg This Weekend that manufacturers are being pushed to sharply increase production, a process complicated by sprawling supply chains and concerns about preserving advanced weapons for other potential conflicts. (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: Trump Says Canada’s Dollar ‘Imbalance’ With US Is Unacceptable
item.description: “Canada’s (currency) Dollar imbalance with the U.S. is unacceptable,” President Donald Trump says in a Truth Social post.
item.dc:creator: Sam Kim

item.title: By The Way: Headlines You May Have Missed
item.description: Taylor Swift and Travis Kelce settling in Ohio, parents teaching teens to invest, what happened to yoga classes, and baseball dogs: Watch Lisa Mateo, Christina Ruffini and Jeff Mason talk about headlines from this week you may have missed on Bloomberg This Weekend! (Source: Bloomberg)

item.title: US Envoys Test New Opening in Ukraine Talks
item.description: US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner arrived in Kyiv for their first official visit to Ukraine after more than three hours of talks with Russian President Vladimir Putin in Moscow produced no announced breakthrough. Joining Bloomberg This Weekend, Bloomberg News Chief Europe Correspondent Oliver Crook says the renewed US effort comes as Ukraine’s deeper strikes into Russia have altered the dynamics of the conflict, while European governments are watching the diplomacy with cautious optimism. (Source: Bloomberg)
